messages:
maya: FYI seeing a spike in push notifications -> lockouts reported by users in <#product>. Okta flagged impossible-travel alerts for several accounts. Anyone on call?
liam: I'm here, pulling Okta and CloudFront logs now.
cheng: quick peek: looks like ~250 MFA pushes across 12 distinct user principals in 8 minutes, source IPs are all over (Rotating NAT / botnet).
okta-bot: [okta] policy:brute_force_protection triggered for 12 users, action: account_lockout (auto)
sarah: any service-accounts affected or only humans?
cheng: primarily humans (customer-facing product and a couple engineers). No service keys touched. 4 accounts already auto-locked and had sessions revoked by policy.
devsec: recommended containment steps: 1) block the source IP ranges at WAF/cloud firewall 2) add temporary Okta sign-on rule to require password+OK 3) revoke active sessions for affected users 4) enable stricter MFA rate-limit policy.
maya: agreed — let's move to containment. Liam, can you create a short blocklist in CloudFront/WAF for the top IP ranges? I have a list in my query.
liam: on it. copying top 10 srcs and submitting WAF change now.
liam: (update) pushed WAF ipset named "sso-push-flood-1934567890" with the top /24 ranges, propagation in ~1m.
infrastructure note (infra-oncall): added temporary deny rule at edge for 3 ranges -> testing propagation.
maya: Cheng, can you revoke sessions for the 12 users and force reauth? Use the admin API.
cheng: doing it. curl snippet I used:
```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: SSWS $OKTA_TOKEN" \
  "https://company.okta.com/api/v1/users/$USER_ID/sessions?inactive=true"
```
cheng: sessions revoked for 12 users, they've been messaged to expect a reauth/email from security.
sarah: I've exported Okta auth logs and put them in the audit bucket: s3://redwood-security/audit/1934567890/okta-logs.json.gz
maya: thanks. Devsec — do we need KMS key rotation or other crypto ops?
devsec: not yet. No indication of key exfil or management plane compromise. Recommend triage first: check if any admin MFA prompts were successful and review console actions. If we find any anomalous token usage, we'll escalate key rotation steps.
liam: scanning cloudtrail for IAM console auths in that window now. If anything suspicious, I'll file an IRT ticket.
maya: next steps: 1) containment done (WAF + session revoke + sign-on rule) 2) communications: send incident note to affected teams + security channel 3) full triage: search logs, confirm no admin compromise 4) follow-up: tighten Okta MFA rate limits + consider adaptive auth.
devsec: assign SEV-2 and create a post-incident checklist item to evaluate persistent blocklist vs. false positives.
maya: assigned to sevs ticket #SEV-2-1934567890 and added follow-up owners: liam (logs), cheng (user comms + sessions), sarah (audit export), devsec (policy hardening).
infra-oncall: leaving the temporary edge rules in place for 6 hours, will monitor for collateral.
liam: preliminary cloudtrail result: no successful console logins from the suspect IP ranges.
cheng: users are back online after reauth, one user reported several suspicious push attempts before lockout — support handled password reset + 2FA re-enroll.
sarah: saved snapshots of Okta admin events to the same audit path.
maya: good progress. we'll keep this open until the postmortem and policy action items are assigned. tagging @devsec for follow-up and adding this to weekly incident review. :white_check_mark:
liam: thanks team. I'll post a short summary once logs finish aggregating.
maya: closing slack thread for now, moving convo into SEV-2 ticket for formal comms.
